1. [IRET.23.1] **Regex engine: RE2.** The regex syntax
   **is** RE2 ([LREG.8.1]) — a commitment of the
   language, not a property of what this runtime links —
   so there is no backend to choose and no swap flag to
   offer: a build option that changed which patterns
   compile, among patterns the runtime accepts at all,
   would make `.ds` source non-portable between conforming
   runtimes. That claim is about swapping engines, not
   about linking one at all — a build carrying no regex
   engine and refusing every DSC that needs one
   ([IRET.23.7]) does not compile a different set of
   patterns than a conforming build with RE2 linked; it
   compiles none.

   PCRE and PCRE2 are excluded: they are backtracking
   engines, and linear-time evaluation is part of what RE2
   buys.

   RE2 is linked on both sides: the runtime matches through
   `ds_re2_compile` / `ds_re2_match`, and the compiler
   validates every pattern with the `google-re2` binding, so
   the two agree on what compiles by construction rather than
   by inspection.
